(mechanic-embodying), the gender-myth-busting node (Thread E · Gender & Respect): a FLAGSHIP of the
strike-and-rewrite signature. "Bust the myth. Write the truth." 90 researched, India-grounded,
EVIDENCE-BASED scenarios across the ability → roles → emotion-&-leadership → "it's just science" →
equality → spot-and-flip arc, each encoded as one of the shared v2 play actions (strike-rewrite / sort /
spot / branch / match / reflect / role-play): no binary "tap the right card". Lead mechanics:
strike-rewrite (bust the myth ×31), sort (fact vs myth ×15), spot (catch the myth ×7). Busts the gender
myths teens hear constantly: ability/brains aren't gendered, roles are cultural not biological, emotion &
leadership aren't male/female traits, the "it's just science" pseudo-science (naturalistic fallacy,
averages-aren't-individuals, cherry-picking, "facts over feelings" shutdowns), and what equality really
means. EVENHANDED, NEVER ANTI-BOY: equality lifts everyone (boys included, less pressure to provide
alone, freedom to feel); boys' real struggles are validated AND equality is championed. Inoculation
against pseudo-science gender claims. Builds on g18 (Norm Storm); prereq g24. Rendered by the shared
engine (components/games/v2-engine.tsx). gameId "mythbuster-lab" (the engine-host registry id; the
GDD/library aspirational id is "mythbuster-gender"). DO NOT RENAME.
title: MythBuster: Gender
greet: It's Lensy. 🧪 Heard a gender 'fact' that didn't sit right? Let's bust the fake science and write the truth: equality lifts everyone, boys included.

badge.title: MythBuster! 🧪
badge.blurb: You can spot a gender myth, see through fake 'just science', and know the truth: ability and roles aren't gendered, and equality frees everyone, boys too. ⚖️

helpLine: Facing unfair treatment or harassment over your gender? You don't have to handle it alone: tell a trusted adult or call Childline on one-zero-nine-eight.

scenarios.hook: "Boys are just naturally better at maths."

myth.un: Boys are naturally better at maths than girls.
myth.re: There's no brain difference in maths ability; the gap is cultural, not biological.
myth.why: Studies find equal maths-brain development, and the gap vanishes where equality is higher.

scenarios.relearn: Boys aren't naturally better at maths; the gap is cultural, not biological.

scenarios.hook: "There's a 'male brain' and a 'female brain'."

myth.un: Brains come in a clear 'male' and 'female' type.
myth.re: Brains overlap hugely; there's no neat male/female split for ability.
myth.why: Individual variation dwarfs any average difference.

scenarios.relearn: There's no tidy 'male brain / female brain'; brains overlap enormously.

scenarios.hook: "Girls can't do science, coding or engineering."

myth.un: Girls just aren't suited to science or engineering.
myth.re: Girls excel in every STEM field; ability isn't gendered.
myth.why: From Kalpana Chawla to top engineers, the proof is everywhere.

scenarios.relearn: Girls excel in STEM; ability there isn't gendered.

scenarios.hook: "Boys can't be good at art, languages or caring work."

myth.un: Boys aren't suited to art, languages or caring roles.
myth.re: Boys excel at all of these; talent has no gender.
myth.why: Limiting boys this way wastes their gifts too.

scenarios.relearn: Boys can excel at art, languages and care; talent has no gender.

scenarios.hook: "Girls are just bad at sport."

myth.un: Girls are naturally bad at sport.
myth.re: Girls are world-class athletes; skill comes from training, not gender.
myth.why: Mary Kom, PV Sindhu and millions more disprove it daily.

scenarios.relearn: Girls are top athletes; sport skill comes from training, not gender.

scenarios.hook: "Men are logical, women are emotional, that's just how brains are."

myth.un: Men are wired for logic, women for emotion.
myth.re: Everyone has both logic and emotion; this binary is a myth.
myth.why: There's no logic-vs-emotion gender switch in the brain.

scenarios.relearn: The 'men=logic, women=emotion' brain split is a myth.

scenarios.hook: "If fewer women are in tech, they must be worse at it."

myth.un: Fewer women in tech proves women are worse at it.
myth.re: Lower numbers come from barriers and bias, not ability.
myth.why: Where barriers drop, women's numbers rise fast.

scenarios.relearn: Fewer women in a field reflects barriers, not lesser ability.

scenarios.hook: "Telling a girl 'girls are bad at maths' is harmless."

myth.un: Saying 'girls are bad at maths' does no harm.
myth.re: Hearing that belief actually lowers girls' maths performance.
myth.why: Stereotypes can become self-fulfilling.

scenarios.relearn: The 'girls are bad at maths' belief itself harms girls' performance.

scenarios.hook: "Boys mature slower, so they just can't focus in school."

myth.un: Boys can't help underperforming; they just mature slower.
myth.re: Expectations and support shape focus far more than gender.
myth.why: Low expectations become an excuse, not a destiny.

scenarios.relearn: Boys' focus depends on support and expectations, not a gender excuse.

scenarios.hook: "A woman's place is in the home."

myth.un: A woman's place is in the home.
myth.re: Women belong wherever they choose, home, work, the world.
myth.why: Homemaking can be a choice, never a destiny imposed by gender.

scenarios.relearn: Women belong wherever they choose; 'a woman's place' is a myth.

scenarios.hook: "A real man is the provider; a man who earns less has failed."

myth.un: A real man must be the main provider.
myth.re: Providing can be shared; a man's worth isn't his pay.
myth.why: This myth crushes boys with pressure too.

scenarios.relearn: Providing is shared; a man's worth isn't his income.

scenarios.hook: "Men can't cook, clean or look after children properly."

myth.un: Men aren't suited to cooking, cleaning or childcare.
myth.re: Men do all of these brilliantly; they're skills, not gender traits.
myth.why: Top chefs and caring dads prove it.

scenarios.relearn: Men can cook, clean and care for kids; these are learned skills.

scenarios.hook: "Some jobs are just men's jobs and some are women's."

myth.un: Jobs are naturally split into men's and women's.
myth.re: Any job can be done by anyone; the split is a made-up custom.
myth.why: Skill, not gender, fits a person to a job.

scenarios.relearn: Jobs aren't gendered; anyone can do any job.

scenarios.hook: "Girls should study less since they'll run a home anyway."

myth.un: Girls need less education; they'll run a home.
myth.re: Every girl deserves a full education and her own future.
myth.why: Education is a right, not a gender privilege.

scenarios.relearn: Girls deserve full education; 'they'll just marry' is a harmful myth.

scenarios.relearn: Sharing housework is fairness, not a favour to women.

scenarios.hook: "Men shouldn't cry; showing emotion is weak."

myth.un: A real man hides his emotions; crying is weak.
myth.re: Everyone feels; expressing emotion is healthy and strong.
myth.why: Bottling up harms boys' mental health.

scenarios.relearn: Men feel and can show emotion; that's strength, not weakness.

myth.re: Understanding emotions makes someone a stronger leader.
myth.why: Emotional skill is a leadership asset, not a flaw.

scenarios.relearn: Emotional skill helps leadership; 'too emotional to lead' is a myth.

scenarios.hook: "Men are just natural leaders."

myth.un: Men are naturally better leaders.
myth.re: Leadership is a skill set anyone can build; gender doesn't grant it.
myth.why: India has had a woman PM and has a woman President.

myth.un: A girl who takes charge is 'bossy'.
myth.re: A girl who takes charge is a leader, same as a boy.
myth.why: The double standard is the only difference.

scenarios.relearn: A girl who leads is a leader, not 'bossy'.

myth.re: Boys are allowed the full range of feelings, like everyone.
myth.why: Only-anger-allowed harms boys and others.

scenarios.hook: "It's just science, men are biologically meant to dominate."

myth.un: Biology means men are meant to dominate.
myth.re: There's no biological law that men must dominate; behaviour is shaped by culture and choice.
myth.why: 'It's natural' never proves something is right or fixed.

scenarios.relearn: No biology makes domination 'natural' or right; choice and culture shape us.

scenarios.hook: "Testosterone makes men aggressive, so it's just their nature."

myth.un: Hormones make men aggressive, so it can't be helped.
myth.re: Hormones nudge, but behaviour is a choice shaped by upbringing.
myth.why: 'My hormones made me' isn't an excuse for how you treat people.

scenarios.relearn: Hormones don't excuse behaviour; how you treat people is a choice.

scenarios.hook: "On average men are X, so every man beats every woman at it."

myth.un: An average difference means every man beats every woman.
myth.re: Averages aren't individuals; the overlap between groups is huge.
myth.why: You can't predict a person from a group average.

scenarios.relearn: Group averages don't decide individuals; overlap is huge.

scenarios.hook: "Cavemen prove men hunt and women stay home, it's evolution."

myth.re: These are just-so stories; real societies have varied wildly.
myth.why: History shows women hunters, leaders and warriors too.

scenarios.relearn: 'Caveman' gender roles are myths; human societies vary hugely.

scenarios.hook: "If a gender difference is natural, it must be good and unchangeable."

myth.re: 'Natural' doesn't mean good or fixed, that's the naturalistic fallacy.
myth.why: Plenty of natural things are harmful; plenty change.

scenarios.relearn: 'Natural' never proves something is good or unchangeable.

scenarios.relearn: There's no logic-brain / feeling-brain split; everyone has both.

scenarios.hook: "Lions let the male eat first, so it's natural for men to come first."

scenarios.relearn: Cherry-picking one animal proves nothing about what's fair for people.

scenarios.relearn: Group averages can't predict an individual; the overlap is huge.

scenarios.relearn: 'Man the hunter' is a just-so story; real human roles varied hugely.

scenarios.hook: "The man's name goes on the house; he's the head of the family."

myth.un: The man is automatically the head of the family.
myth.re: A family can be led together, as equal partners.

scenarios.relearn: A family can be led together, not headed by one gender by default.

scenarios.hook: "A daughter is paraya dhan; her real home is her in-laws'."

myth.un: A daughter belongs to her future in-laws, not her own family.
myth.re: A daughter belongs to herself and is family for life.
myth.why: 'Paraya dhan' is an old custom, not a fact about her worth.

scenarios.relearn: A daughter is not 'someone else's'; she's family for life.

scenarios.hook: "A son must carry the family forward; a daughter just leaves."

myth.un: Only a son can carry the family's name and future forward.
myth.re: A daughter can carry a family forward just as fully.
myth.why: Care, name and legacy aren't decided by gender.

scenarios.relearn: A daughter can carry a family forward as much as a son.

scenarios.hook: "If a wife earns more than her husband, something's wrong."

myth.un: A wife shouldn't earn more than her husband.
myth.re: Whoever earns more, a fair home shares the load and the say.
myth.why: Income doesn't rank partners; respect isn't a pay slip.

scenarios.relearn: Either partner can earn more; it doesn't make the home unequal.

scenarios.hook: "A stay-at-home dad is just lazy or unemployed."

myth.un: A dad who stays home with the kids is being lazy.
myth.re: Running a home and raising kids is real, full-time work.
myth.why: Care work is work, whoever does it.

scenarios.relearn: A stay-at-home dad is doing real work, not avoiding it.

scenarios.hook: "A real man should never have to ask his wife for help at home."

myth.un: A real man manages without asking his wife for help.
myth.re: Asking for help and sharing tasks is partnership, not weakness.
myth.why: This 'lone provider' myth piles pressure on boys too.

scenarios.relearn: Sharing and asking for help at home is strength, not weakness.

scenarios.hook: "Girls take home science; boys take woodwork. That's just how it is."

myth.un: Girls belong in home science and boys in workshops.
myth.re: Any student can pick cooking, sewing, woodwork or wiring.
myth.why: Subjects suit interests, not a gender.

scenarios.relearn: School subjects aren't gendered; pick by interest, not by 'girls/boys'.

scenarios.hook: "Looking after elderly parents is the daughter-in-law's duty."

myth.un: Caring for ageing parents falls to the daughter-in-law.
myth.re: Every grown child can share the care of their parents.
myth.why: Sons can cook, nurse and sit up at night too.

scenarios.relearn: Caring for elders is every child's job, not one woman's duty.

scenarios.hook: "Serve the men first; the women eat after."

myth.re: Everyone at the table can eat together, equally.
myth.why: Who eats first isn't a rule of nature, just a habit.

scenarios.relearn: Eating order isn't a gender rule; a family can share the table.

scenarios.hook: "A girl who can't cook will never manage her own home."

myth.re: Anyone can learn to cook; it isn't a test of being a girl.
myth.why: Boys need the same kitchen skills for their own lives.

scenarios.relearn: Cooking is a life skill for all, not a girl's pass-or-fail test.

scenarios.hook: "Driving the family car is the husband's job."

myth.un: The husband is the one who should drive the family.
myth.re: Whoever drives best or is free can take the wheel.
myth.why: Driving is a skill anyone can learn, regardless of gender.

scenarios.relearn: Driving the family isn't a husband's job; any licensed adult can.

scenarios.hook: "Boys shouldn't do the dishes; that's the girls' chore."

myth.un: Dishes and cleaning are chores for the girls of the house.
myth.re: Chores belong to whoever lives there, shared fairly.
myth.why: A clean home is everyone's job, not one gender's.

scenarios.relearn: Household chores are shared by all who live there, boys included.

scenarios.hook: "A working mum is neglecting her children."

myth.re: A dad caring for his child is just parenting, not a bonus.
myth.why: We don't call a mum 'amazing' for the same basic care.

scenarios.relearn: A dad caring for his child is normal parenting, not a favour.

scenarios.hook: "A wife should always put her own dreams last."

myth.un: A wife's own dreams must come after everyone else's.
myth.re: A partner's dreams matter too; a fair home makes room for both.
myth.why: Sacrifice can be shared, not assigned by gender.

scenarios.relearn: Both partners' dreams count; one gender doesn't always go last.

scenarios.hook: "Tailoring and stitching are women's work."

myth.un: Sewing and tailoring are jobs for women.
myth.re: Tailoring is a skilled trade open to anyone; many master tailors are men.
myth.why: Skill at the machine isn't decided by gender.

scenarios.relearn: Tailoring is a skilled trade for anyone, not 'women's work'.

scenarios.hook: "A man crying in front of his kids loses their respect."

myth.re: A dad who shows real feeling teaches his kids it's okay to feel.

scenarios.relearn: A dad showing feelings models healthy emotion, not lost respect.

scenarios.hook: "A girl studying engineering is taking a boy's seat."

myth.why: Skill, not gender, decides who belongs in a field.

scenarios.relearn: No field belongs to one gender; a seat goes to talent, not boys.

myth.re: Marriage doesn't end anyone's right to work and grow.
